newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich promises to personally repay Dole loan.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich promises to personally repay Dole loan.

text.p: WASHINGTON, April 17 (Reuter - House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich on Thursday promised Congress he will personally repay a $300,000 loan from Bob Dole to settle an ethics penalty, vowing, "taxpayers will be fully reimbursed."

In a speech to the House explaining the surprise development that Dole, the losing 1996 Republican presidential candidate, would finance his debt, Gingrich said: "I will personally pay it back. The taxpayers will be fully reimbursed ... This is my duty as speaker and I will do it personally."

The speech followed the stunning announcement that Dole would lend Gingrich the entire amout to defray a penalty levied by the House for ethics violations in a vote in January. His remarks were clearly designed to head off speculation he might use political funds to pay the Dole loan.

He insisted his ethics violations had been essentially technical ones in the first place -- a view contested by many House colleagues -- and that the law would have allowed him to pay the penalty from either campaign funds or a legal defense fund.

But he said he and his wife, Marianne, "came to the conclusion of our own choice ... that I have a moral obligation to pay the $300,000 out of personal funds, that any other choice would simply be seen as one more politician shirking his duty."

"Therefore, as a person of limited means, I have arranged to borrow the money from Bob Dole ... and I will personally pay it back," he said. The penalty was to reimburse the House for taxpayer funds expended in investigating charges Gingrich used tax-exempt money to promote political goals and misled congressional investigators.
Dole issued a statement saying he was glad to lend Gingrich the money as a friend and for the good of their Republican party. Tax records show he and his wife Elizabeth are multimillionaires.
